input_references.role: Completed driver orders with request, pickup, and drop-off events
Afternoon citywide order events, including orders served by the target driver and by other taxis
All-taxi requests at Central Arena Stand, including other drivers
Timestamped GPS points and point speeds for driver segments

metadata.goal: Analyze how a taxi driver’s operating strategy changes over two months of observed work, and assess whether the changes are consistent with learning from recurring demand and route conditions.
metadata.category: Experience-conditioned driver strategy, market discovery, and route execution
metadata.header: Two Months of Driver Strategy Adaptation
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed single-driver Porto Taxi case spanning June and July. Driver activity, linked GPS trajectories, citywide afternoon orders, Friday labels, and all-taxi C-stand request records support comparisons between early and later operating periods.
metadata.motion_consistency_note: Point speed is the incoming segment GPS great-circle distance divided by elapsed time; the first point repeats the first outgoing segment speed. Earth radius: 6371.0088 km. Trip distance is the sum of these segment distances. avg_speed_kmh and mean_speed_kmh are total distance / elapsed time; avg_point_speed_kmh and point_speed_mean_kmh are unweighted means of the delivered point speeds. speed_cv is the population coefficient of variation of incoming segment speeds, excluding the duplicated first endpoint. trajectory_progress is point_index / (point_count - 1), not elapsed-time fraction. Timestamps and speed fields were reconstructed for internal consistency on 2026-10-09; GPS positions and insight wording were preserved. These are curated example records, not newly recovered observations.

operating_state_definitions.cruising: Unassigned movement while seeking an order; the segment has nonzero GPS displacement along its path.
operating_state_definitions.idle_wait: Stationary, unassigned availability interval; no accepted order is linked.
operating_state_definitions.driving_to_pickup: Movement to the pickup location after accepting an order.
operating_state_definitions.pickup_wait: Stationary interval at the pickup location between request and passenger pickup, linked to an accepted order.
operating_state_definitions.passenger_trip: Passenger service between pickup and drop-off.
operating_state_definitions.taxi_stand_wait: Stationary availability at the taxi stand before the next accepted order, distinct from pickup_wait.

metadata.stand_market_linkage_note: In this curated case, taxi_id in stand_market_requests identifies the taxi assigned to the request. All target-driver stand requests are completed and join one-to-one to driver_orders on taxi_id=driver_id and parsed request_time, with matching date, period and request_source. Other-taxi requests have no delivered driver-order details. market_request_id is a stable opaque record identifier, not an encoded event clock. approach_segment_id links the pre-pickup interval, which may be driving_to_pickup or stationary pickup_wait. The 2026-10-09 repair corrected constructed assignments and copied request times from the latest completed orders.

insight_list.insight: The driver’s afternoon activity shifts from broad cruising to a more concentrated pattern around recurring service areas.

plot.title: From Broad Cruising to an A–B Service Focus
plot.description: Trajectory maps and separate 13:00–18:00 pickup/drop-off maps contrast early citywide exploration with later A–B concentration.

insight_list.question: How do the driver’s 13:00–18:00 cruising paths and street-hail order locations change from the early to later period, and what recurring A–B pattern is visible early?

insight_list.insight: On Friday evenings, the driver’s activity becomes more focused on a taxi stand, with longer waits in the later period.

plot.title: Friday C-Stand Demand and Later Waiting
plot.description: All-taxi market requests establish the Friday stand-demand pattern; the driver timeline compares early and later Friday behavior.

insight_list.question: What does the all-taxi request data show about Central Arena Stand demand on Friday evenings, and how does the driver’s behavior at the stand change later?

insight_list.insight: Morning trips in the later period are faster and have more stable speed profiles, while route indirectness remains similar.

plot.title: Morning Route Execution across Observation Periods (06:00–09:00)
plot.description: Point-speed profiles and trip summaries compare route indirectness, speed level, and speed stability across the two observation periods.

insight_list.question: For trips made between 06:00 and 09:00, how do route indirectness, speed level, and speed stability compare between the early and later observation periods?

insights: The driver’s afternoon activity shifts from broad cruising to a more concentrated pattern around recurring service areas.
On Friday evenings, the driver’s activity becomes more focused on a taxi stand, with longer waits in the later period.
Morning trips in the later period are faster and have more stable speed profiles, while route indirectness remains similar.
summary: Over two observed months, this driver’s behavior changes in ways consistent with learning recurring market and route conditions. Later 13:00–18:00 work remains centered on the A–B street-hail pair despite a smaller set of non-A/B orders; later Friday evenings involve substantially longer C-stand waiting; and later indirect morning trips are steadier while maintaining a relatively high speed level.
